title_hi: बिंदुसार: अशोक के पिता की कहानी
title_en: Bindusara: The Story of Ashoka's Father

full.title: ज़हर की बूंद से पैदा हुआ राजा, जिसके बेटे ने गद्दी छीनी | Bindusara Mauryan Emperor Full Story

about_en: The full story of Bindusara, the second Mauryan emperor, son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of Ashoka the Great. It covers the poison-drop birth legend, his Greek name Amitrochates, Taranatha's claim of 16 conquered towns, Chanakya's death and the fight between Sushima and Ashoka over the throne.
about_hi:
बिंदुसार: ज़हर की एक बूंद से मिला नाम, और गद्दी उस बेटे को जिसे वह पसंद नहीं करता था।
चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के बेटे और सम्राट अशोक के पिता की पूरी कहानी, शॉर्ट्स से कहीं ज़्यादा गहराई में।
जैन और बौद्ध कथाएँ, तिब्बती इतिहासकार तारानाथ और ग्रीक लेखक, सब अलग अलग बातें कहते हैं।
इस सीरीज़ के सारे शॉर्ट्स प्लेलिस्ट "बिंदुसार – ज़हर, चाणक्य और गद्दी की जंग | Bindusara – Poison, Chanakya and the Throne" में देखिए।
facts: Bindusara (r. c. 297 – c. 273 BCE) was the second Mauryan emperor, son of Chandragupta and father of Ashoka; most of what we know about him comes from legends written centuries after his death.

Name legend: Jain and Buddhist texts say Chanakya fed Chandragupta small doses of poison, and the pregnant queen ate some by mistake. In the Buddhist version the baby was kept for seven days in the bellies of freshly killed goats and was named for the goat-blood spots (bindu). In Hemachandra's Jain version, a drop of poison touched the baby's head, so the name means 'strength of the drop'. The queen's name there is Durdhara.

Greek writers called him Amitrochates or Allitrochades, probably from the Sanskrit title Amitraghata, 'slayer of enemies'. He was also called Devanampriya, and one Jain text says his birth name was Simhasena.

Taranatha (16th century) says Chanakya destroyed the nobles and kings of 16 towns and made Bindusara master of the land between the western and eastern seas. Historians disagree on whether this means conquest of the Deccan, crushing revolts, or just holding what he inherited.

Hemachandra's legend: the minister Subandhu, out of jealousy, told Bindusara that Chanakya had cut open his mother's belly. Bindusara turned against Chanakya, then regretted it. Subandhu pretended to make peace with Chanakya and burned him to death, and Chanakya's curse later forced Subandhu to become a monk.

Bindusara was on friendly terms with the Greeks. Athenaeus, quoting Hegesander, says he asked Antiochus I for sweet wine, dried figs and a sophist. Antiochus agreed to the wine and figs but said Greek law forbade selling a sophist.

In the Ashokavadana, Bindusara favoured Sushima and disliked Ashoka. Minister Khallataka and the 500 councillors backed Ashoka. While Sushima was failing to crush a revolt in Takshashila, the angry, dying king saw the crown placed on Ashoka's head, and Radhagupta later tricked Sushima into a pit of burning charcoal.
Other sources disagree: the Brahmanda Purana says Bindusara crowned Ashoka himself, and the Rajavali-Katha says he retired after handing Ashoka the throne.

parts.title: भाग 1: ज़हर की एक बूंद से मिला नाम बिंदुसार? | Bindusara
parts.topic: ज़हर की एक बूंद से मिला नाम 'बिंदुसार'?
parts.hook: जैन किताबें कहती हैं, बिंदुसार को मरी माँ का पेट चीरकर निकाला गया। चंद्रगुप्त का बेटा, अशोक का पिता।

parts.title: भाग 2: 16 नगरों के राजा खत्म, फिर नफ़रत? | Bindusara
parts.topic: 16 नगरों के राजा खत्म, फिर चाणक्य से नफ़रत?
parts.hook: सोलह नगरों के सामंत और राजा, चाणक्य ने बिंदुसार के लिए मिटा दिए। ऐसा तिब्बती लेखक तारानाथ लिखते हैं। बिंदुसार, चंद्रगुप्त का बेटा और अशोक का पिता।

parts.title: भाग 3: ग्रीक राजा से मांगी 3 चीज़ें, 1 पर मिला इनकार | Bindusara
parts.topic: ग्रीक राजा से मांगी 3 चीज़ें, 1 पर मिला इनकार
parts.hook: बिंदुसार ने ग्रीक राजा से तीन चीज़ें मांगीं। एक पर जवाब आया, हमारा क़ानून बेचने नहीं देता।

parts.title: भाग 4: पिता चाहते थे सुशीमा, ताज मिला अशोक को? | Bindusara
parts.topic: पिता चाहते थे सुशीमा, ताज मिला अशोक को?
parts.hook: मौत के बिस्तर पर बिंदुसार बोले, राजा सुशीमा बनेगा। पर मंत्री, अशोक के साथ थे।
